rules.title: Concurrency is the `Core\Task` roster over the runtime's own single scheduler
rules.divergesFromPhp: a PHP request has no concurrency to express at all, and the nearest equivalents — `curl_multi_*`, `pcntl_fork`, an extension's own event loop — have no counterpart here

rules.title: `Core\Task::all` answers a shape with the argument's own field names, each field keeping its own type
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no PHP construct that runs several calls at once and hands back their results already typed

rules.title: An `all` field binds its type from a written `fn` literal, and a `callable` variable there is a compile error naming the field
Every task is a child of the task that started it, shares that request's accounting, and dies with it
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP has no task, so it has no orphan either; here an unparented task is impossible rather than discouraged

rules.title: `Core\Task::map` answers an array of the callback's own return type, in the input's keys and order
rules.divergesFromPhp: `array_map` runs sequentially; this one runs the callback concurrently and still answers in the input's order

rules.title: `{limit, deadline}` is the whole of what bounds a group, and there is no `timeout` member and no `race`
rules.divergesFromPhp: a wait is bounded by an option on the call rather than by `set_time_limit`, `default_socket_timeout` or an ini setting read from somewhere else

rules.title: Control never leaves `all` or `map` with a child still running
rules.divergesFromPhp: a PHP script that starts something in the background has no construct that waits for it, so nothing there guarantees this

rules.title: A deadline bounds when cancellation is asked for, not when the call returns
A cancelled task runs no `catch`, no cleanup and no handler, and cancellation is not a `Throwable`
rules.divergesFromPhp: the `finally`-shaped cleanup a PHP developer would reach for does not run, and there is nothing to catch

rules.title: `Core\Task::afterResponse` runs after the request's own frame returns, still charged to the request tree
rules.divergesFromPhp: `fastcgi_finish_request` keeps the whole worker busy with no accounting, no cap and no deadline; this keeps the tree, and the tree is still bounded

rules.title: Only the request's own task may defer work, and deferred work may not defer more
Deferred work may read the request but not write the response, and its uncaught throw reaches the log alone
rules.divergesFromPhp: output written after `fastcgi_finish_request` is silently discarded; here it is refused, at compile time where the call is statically visible

rules.title: `[deferred]` carries two bounds: a `System` `max_concurrent` and a `Runtime` `deadline`
Past `[deferred] max_concurrent`, `afterResponse` throws at the call site rather than queueing
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no queue in front of this and no silent backlog; overload is reported to the request that caused it

rules.title: A value outlives the request that made it only by being put into a named store
rules.divergesFromPhp: APCu, `shmop`, `sysvshm`, `sysvsem` and `sysvmsg` are gone, and there is no ambient place a value can be left for the next request to find

rules.title: A value is copied into the cache and copied back out, by the same graph copy the isolate boundary uses
rules.divergesFromPhp: APCu's serialize-on-store is a wire format with its own type losses; this is the language's own copy, and it refuses what may not cross rather than mangling it

rules.title: The cache boundary is a copy in and a copy out, so nothing across it is read-modify-write
rules.divergesFromPhp: `apcu_add`, `apcu_cas` and `apcu_inc` have no counterpart, so a lock or a counter is not built on the cache at all

rules.title: The local tier's memory is charged to the core, capped in `nvs.toml`, and the cap evicts rather than failing a write
rules.divergesFromPhp: `apc.shm_size` exhaustion makes a store fail; here the cap forgets an older entry and the write succeeds

rules.title: Anything a program relies on the value of goes to the shared tier, and the local tier is not offered for it
rules.divergesFromPhp: an APCu-backed session, lock or rate limit does not port: the local tier is not among the backends, so the miswiring is a configuration error rather than a race

rules.title: A persistent connection is a root isolate, and the request that upgraded it ends
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is nothing a PHP process can hold across requests, so a connection has no counterpart at all — and it is a root rather than a request that never ends

rules.title: An upgrade names compiled code — a file or a static method — and never a closure
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no handler object and no closure to hand a socket to; the entry is named at the call site the way a spawned script names one, and its arguments are copied rather than shared

rules.title: An upgrade's `args`, `limits`, `grants` and `on` are a spawned script's options as ordinary named arguments
Inside a connection, code is an ordinary loop, and `receive()` answering `null` is what ends it
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `onMessage` callback and no event registration — suspension has no colour, so a blocking-shaped `while` is the whole program

rules.title: `receive()` is the one wait, and it answers the peer or a subscribed topic, whichever arrives first
What a peer sent arrives `tainted`, and `Core\Validate` is the only way to launder it
rules.divergesFromPhp: a frame is untrusted by type rather than by convention, so it reaches no sink until it has been validated

rules.title: A stream that ends with its response is a streaming response; one that outlives it is a connection isolate
rules.divergesFromPhp: the choice is made by lifetime rather than by protocol, and there is no `flush`-in-a-loop shape that keeps a request alive

rules.title: `Core\Socket` and `Core\Sse` are two hand-overs onto one isolate, and each reports the one it is missing
Every bound on an open connection is finite with nothing configured
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no unbounded wait to configure your way into: an idle, a lifetime and a send timeout all apply before any configuration is written

rules.title: An open connection runs to completion on the code it started with, and an edit reaches only the next one
rules.divergesFromPhp: a deploy does not break what is open — there is no per-request re-read of a file a live connection is standing in

rules.title: A shutdown or a reload closes a connection with a defined code after a drain, never with a reset
A connection is one future, driven to completion by the coroutine that owns it
A waker decides nothing; it is permission to make one more poll happen
One wake permission is installed per drive, and a fresh one is issued only after it fires
A wake from another core queues an id on the task's own core and never migrates it
A cancellation ends the drive: torn down where it parked, or told once and answered
Where a drive parks is decided once when it starts, and off a core it blocks the thread
A `push` on the queue's connection commits with the write that caused it, or neither happens
rules.divergesFromPhp: a queued job and the database write that justified it commit together, where an application on a broker writes an outbox row and relays it afterwards

rules.title: `Core\Queue` is four members, and each is asked about a job or about a queue, never about a row number
rules.divergesFromPhp: the queue is four members of the runtime rather than a framework façade, and what `push` answers is a handle rather than an integer id

rules.title: A job between attempts is `Pending`, and there is no `Failed` state to ask about
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no failed state to poll for — a job waiting out its backoff is indistinguishable from one that has not run yet, and "did it fail" is a question about the dead-letter table

rules.title: `cancel` answers whether it won the race, and it changes the job's state rather than deleting the row
rules.divergesFromPhp: cancelling is a race against a worker rather than a command, and the answer says which side won it

rules.title: A job names a script file, and its payload crosses as a copied value
rules.divergesFromPhp: a job is a file rather than a class implementing an interface, and nothing about it is a serialized object graph waiting to be reconstructed

rules.title: A job's budget and grants are recorded when it is enqueued, and narrowed from that context rather than widened
rules.divergesFromPhp: background work carries its own memory, CPU and time budget, and its permissions can only shrink from those of the code that enqueued it

rules.title: A worker claims a job with one statement the database arbitrates, so a fleet needs no lease protocol
rules.divergesFromPhp: a fleet needs no supervisor, no heartbeat and no coordinator process — the database provides the mutual exclusion

rules.title: Delivery is at-least-once, and idempotency is the job's own obligation
rules.divergesFromPhp: the guarantee is stated rather than implied, so a job is written to tolerate running twice instead of assuming it will not

rules.title: Attempts are finite, backoff is exponential and jittered, and an exhausted job is kept rather than discarded
rules.divergesFromPhp: nothing is discarded silently and nothing retries forever — an exhausted job is a row in a dead-letter table rather than a line in a log

rules.title: A job that exceeds its budget is a failed attempt, reported as that and retried like any other
rules.divergesFromPhp: exhausting memory in background work is a bounded failed attempt rather than a fatal that takes the process with it

rules.title: A job runs as a root isolate, and there is no second execution path
rules.divergesFromPhp: a job shares nothing with the request that enqueued it — no statics, no session, no superglobals — because it is a fresh isolate rather than the same process continuing

rules.title: Which process runs a job is configuration, and every spelling drives the identical isolate
rules.divergesFromPhp: workers are the runtime's own and start from configuration — there is no separate daemon or process manager to install beside the server

rules.title: A durable payload refuses `secret`, and a `tainted` value comes back `tainted`
rules.divergesFromPhp: a credential cannot enter a job payload at all, and taint survives the round trip through the database instead of being laundered by it

rules.title: A `push` on a connection other than the queue's is not transactional, and is counted rather than assumed away
rules.divergesFromPhp: losing atomicity between a write and its job is a measured deployment fact rather than an unstated one

rules.title: Queued work is durable, retried and declared by the application; scheduled work is a clock tick and none of those
rules.divergesFromPhp: cron-style entries and background jobs are two mechanisms with two guarantees, rather than one worker loop doing both

rules.title: There is no broker backend and no pluggable driver, because a driver makes transactional enqueue optional
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no Redis, SQS or AMQP backend to choose and nothing to configure between the application and its jobs

rules.title: The reactor reports readiness on every platform, Windows included, so a stream is written once
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no event loop to install and no extension to pick — readiness is the runtime's own and behaves the same on all three platforms

rules.title: A task registers before it suspends, treats a wake as a hint, and leaves the reactor holding nothing when it ends
rules.divergesFromPhp: a request that waits on I/O suspends one task and hands its core to another, rather than occupying a process until the kernel answers

rules.title: A stream issues the syscall first and parks only on `WouldBlock`, so a warm socket pays nothing
rules.divergesFromPhp: a read that would block suspends the task rather than the process, and a socket with bytes already buffered costs one ordinary syscall

rules.title: A parking stream is a plain `Read` and `Write`, so nothing up the call chain is coloured
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `await` and no second spelling of any member that touches I/O — a helper reads a socket with the call it would use on a blocking one

rules.title: A task's stack is 1 MiB of reserved address space, resident only where it is touched, and pooled per worker
rules.divergesFromPhp: concurrency costs a stack rather than a process, so one machine holds tasks in the hundred-thousands instead of workers in the hundreds

rules.title: A task's recursion limit is armed from the real bounds of the stack it was handed
rules.divergesFromPhp: deep recursion throws a catchable error at a bound derived from the actual stack, rather than crashing the process or being counted by a configured depth alone
